results.title: Fleet-Level Optimization for Heterogeneous Device Provisioning in ML Model Deployments
results.venue: International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems Workshops
results.abstract: With the increasing popularity of machine learning (ML) applications, networked computing systems like cloud data-centres are facing rapidly growing demand for ML inference tasks. Expanding systems to meet these demands, however, can be both costly and environmentally unsustainable. While several computer architecture optimizations have been proposed to alleviate monetary and environmental costs, e.g., by reusing older devices or those less customized to ML workloads, the resulting cost and performance tradeoffs at a platform level have yet to be modelled. We have also observed a structure to inference latency, i.e. a single prefill phase and a decode phase of an a priori unknown number of repeated computations. For LLMs, the computation time of an inference task (dominated by output token inference) is correlated with the length of its input [1]. As shorter-input requests tend to return fewer tokens, it is possible to isolate these tasks and allocate them on dedicated devices; indeed, a form of this segmenting currently occurs in deployment. As such, it is possible to use older or slower computation units to handle this segment of demand.
